messages:
anita: uploaded a quick Figma of the compact threshold rows + notification preview. main ask: do we trim copy in the preview or keep full channel names? also worried about what screen readers will announce when suppressions toggle on/off.

jess: i lean toward truncating long channel names in the compact view with a tooltip for full name. keeps density. :+1:

mike: agreed on tooltip. question: when a suppression is active, should the preview show 'suppressed' badge inline or a separate header?

anita: my mock shows inline badge to keep association with the individual channel, but it does eat horizontal space. header could be clearer for people scanning for suppression state.

ryan: header is easier for keyboard users to jump to, but inline badge helps when multiple channels have mixed states. maybe both? small compact badge plus a summary header count.

olga: accessibility nit — if we keep inline badges, make sure aria-labels read like "Email channel, suppressed until 3pm" instead of just "suppressed". screen readers need context.

sam: copy tweak: change "suppress" button to "snooze notifications" in the preview. more user-friendly.
jess: hmm i like "snooze" for product copy but internal config screens usually use "suppress". can we test readability?
mike: i sketched a microcopy table in the doc: UI label vs tooltip vs aria text. recommend "Snooze (suppress notifications)" for new users.

anita: good call. i'll update mocks. quick accessibility question: a11y-bot says avoid live region floods. if toggling suppression triggers many live announcements, that's bad.

a11y-bot: Recommendation: use polite aria-live on the summary header and avoid live regions on each row. update announcement text to be concise, e.g., "Notification snoozed for Email until 15:00".

ryan: also consider focus management when users open the preview panel. focus should land on the first interactive control, not the header only. keyboard flow otherwise stalls.

olga: accessible tooltip suggestion: expose the full channel name as an accessible name on hover/focus, not just visual tooltip. use aria-describedby to the hidden full-name element.

sam: one more small UX thing — when we truncate channel names, add a subtle avatar/icon so users can disambiguate channels quickly.
jess: teams with many channels will appreciate the icon. +1.
mike: implementation note for eng: if we show summary header + inline microbadges, we need to avoid duplicating suppression toggles that can get out of sync. better to have header controls affect all rows and keep per-row toggle as independent. sync logic belongs in the controller layer.
anita: thanks. i'll update the Figma: "summary header with count", "inline microbadges with concise aria", "truncate with accessible full-name" and copy suggestion "Snooze (suppress notifications)".

a11y-bot: Quick accessibility checklist: 1) polite aria-live on header; 2) aria-labels include channel + state; 3) focus lands on first control; 4) tooltips exposed to screen readers.

jess: timeline — can we get updated frames by EOD? i'd like UX review before dev picks it up.
anita: yep i'll push updates by 5pm and drop the new link here. thanks everyone! :rocket:
